h1: Patt Serviced Apartments — a serviced apartment with a pool and gym inside Amata Nakorn estate that suits estate workers, long-stay guests, and families who want a condo-style room
intro: If you're looking for somewhere to stay in the Amata Nakorn area of Chonburi that isn't an ordinary by-the-night hotel but a "condo-style room you can actually live in for several days, with a pool and gym to use, easy parking, and both daily and monthly rates", Patt Serviced Apartments is a name worth keeping on your list · it's a condo-style serviced apartment at 471/249 Moo 5, Soi Thonglang, Khlong Tamru, Mueang Chon Buri, in the heart of Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate, about a 15-minute walk from the Amata Nakorn estate · what guests bring up most often is clean, roomy condo-style rooms of around 34 sqm, a free outdoor pool and gym, free parking, and a kitchenette with a dining nook in some rooms, which suits people working in the Amata estate, families relocating to Chonburi for several months, and self-drivers who want a comfortable room on a manageable budget · it takes both daily and monthly stays, with daily rates from about THB 720/night and monthly rates from about THB 9,000 and up depending on room type and length of stay · scored 8.3 from 34 reviews on Trip.com

body.html: Who Patt Serviced Apartments is for — to put it as briefly as possible, Patt Serviced Apartments is a condo-style serviced apartment for people who want "a clean room, private space, and somewhere they can actually live in for several days" in the Amata Nakorn industrial area, rather than a beachfront resort feel or sea views · it isn't a beachfront hotel where you step out of your room onto the sand, and it doesn't lean on luxe boutique design · instead it's a condo-style residential building designed to be genuinely livable, both by the day and by the month, with an outdoor pool and gym that many apartments in the same price range simply don't have · real reviews line up on the point that the people it suits are workers in the Amata Nakorn estate who need to live in Chonburi for months at a time, company staff and engineers on projects, families relocating temporarily, and self-drivers who want a spacious room with everything they need at a lighter price than a full-service hotel · another group who find it worth it is people running errands around the estate for several days who want a place with a kitchenette to cook for themselves, a pool to unwind in after work, and parking they don't have to fight over · in plain terms, this place plays on "living comfortably, like your own condo near work" on a budget that works for a long stay in Chonburi, while anyone chasing a beach trip or a relaxed seaside vibe may find it doesn't match what they're after, because the building sits on the industrial estate side, not the beach zone.

Location and getting around — Patt Serviced Apartments sits at 471/249 Moo 5, Soi Thonglang, Khlong Tamru, Mueang Chon Buri, within Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate · the thing to understand before booking is that this is accommodation in an industrial area, not a beach district, with the building sitting near clusters of factories and major companies, which makes it a location suited mainly to people working in the estate · from the property it's about a 15-minute walk to the Amata Nakorn estate, and it's within walking distance of Ninja Night Market too, the local evening eating-and-hanging-out spot · there are convenience stores, made-to-order eateries and markets all around for everyday life, while for shopping and big malls it's about a 15-minute drive to Central Chonburi · longer trips are still convenient because it's near the Bang Na–Trat (Burapha Withi) expressway that connects Bangkok, Pattaya and Rayong · Bangsaen Beach is within driving distance from the property, and you can carry on south to Pattaya · for airports, it's about 40 km from Suvarnabhumi Airport, or roughly a 50-minute drive, and Chonburi train station is about 10 km away · the honest observation is that this place suits people with a car or estate workers who commute regularly more than general tourists, because it's in a soi on the estate side, and without your own car, hailing a ride here may not be as easy or as frequent as in the city or the Bangsaen Beach zone, so plan your transport ahead.

"Clean, roomy, nice atmosphere, with a kitchenette so you can cook for yourself, head down for a swim after work and then hit the gym, parking is easy and you don't have to fight for it. It really suits us, coming to work in the Amata estate and having to stay long-term for months."

Room types and decor — Patt is a condo-style building that splits its rooms into several tiers to choose from based on budget, number of people, and length of stay · most rooms are around 34 square meters, which is more generous than a standard hotel room · it starts with the Superior Room, a king-bed room for daily stays, good for a solo traveler or a couple who want more space than a small hotel room · stepping up there's the Deluxe Room, geared toward monthly stays for long-term guests, the Junior Suite, available both with and without a bathtub, and the largest rooms, the Family Suite and the two-bedroom room (2 Bedroom), suited to families or groups traveling together · what sets this place apart from an ordinary apartment is the in-room amenities geared for long stays — many rooms have a fridge, microwave, satellite TV, safe, and some have a kitchenette with a sofa and dining nook · many rooms have a private balcony · the decor leans toward a bright, clean modern-condo tone, nothing flashy but tidy and comfortable to live in · most real reviews agree that the rooms are clean, roomy, have a nice atmosphere, and come well equipped for long stays, which is what estate workers and monthly guests care about most · a recurring observation is that some reviews mention a cigarette smell in certain rooms and bathroom drains that are sometimes slow, so check the room's condition at check-in and tell staff right away if you find a problem, to ask for a room change or a fix before you settle in, especially if you plan to stay long.

Facilities, pool and gym — what sets Patt apart from many apartments in the same price range is that it has a free outdoor pool and gym to use · both the pool and gym are open 6:00 AM–10:00 PM daily, so estate workers who finish in the evening can still go down for a relaxing swim or a workout · some reviews mention it's a saltwater pool, which is gentler on skin and eyes than a typical chlorine pool · on top of that there's a clubhouse as a common area to sit and relax, free parking that many reviews say is convenient and not a fight, which matters for self-drivers and estate workers, a convenience store/shop in the building, a laundry service (paid) that helps a lot with long stays, a 24-hour front desk, and free Wi-Fi in the rooms and common areas · for actual day-to-day living, this set of facilities counts as complete for someone staying many days or months — somewhere to work out, somewhere to swim and unwind, somewhere to do laundry, shops close by, and parking · so the strength here isn't "luxury-resort facilities" but a set of things that genuinely get used in daily life, which fits the lifestyle of estate workers and long-stay guests more squarely.

Food and places around — Patt has an in-building restaurant for lunch, a cafe/coffee shop and room service during limited hours, but this isn't a place you come to mainly to eat at the hotel · most of the information and the reviews don't emphasize a hotel-style buffet breakfast, so set your expectations that meals will rely mainly on the places around and on cooking for yourself in the room, which is normal for a serviced apartment · the upside is the Amata Nakorn area has made-to-order eateries, rice shops, cafes and convenience stores all around within walking and short driving distance, plus Ninja Night Market within walking distance, the local evening eating-and-hanging-out spot with single-plate dishes, fried snacks, grilled food and drinks · for long-stay guests, the fact that many rooms have a kitchenette, fridge and microwave means you can easily buy groceries to cook or reheat in the room, which saves money and gives far more flexibility around meals than an ordinary hotel, especially for workers who want a simple meal after work without going out every time · if you want to seriously dig into Chonburi's signature food, you can drive out to Nong Mon Market for souvenirs and seafood, or head into Central Chonburi with its restaurants and food court · overall, food at Patt is about "relying on the places around and cooking for yourself easily" more than being a selling point of the property itself.

Service and care — service at Patt is overall at a level guests are happy with, and it's one of the sub-scores that does well on booking platforms (a service score of around 8.5 on Trip.com) · real reviews mention attentive staff who respond well to things and help make the stay smooth, with a 24-hour front desk that lets shift workers or late arrivals check in · the point to say plainly is that some voices in reviews note that housekeeping knocks to clean in the morning around 8 without giving notice, which night-shift workers or anyone wanting to sleep in may find disruptive · some guests suggest telling staff your preferred cleaning time or asking to hang a do-not-disturb sign right from check-in, so the room-entry schedule matches when it's convenient for you · this is common at serviced apartments with regular cleaning service and is usually fixed by communicating clearly with the front desk · overall, if you set your expectations correctly that this is a serviced apartment geared for long stays rather than a full-service hotel, most of the experience goes well.

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — gathered from Trip.com, TripAdvisor and other booking platforms, the picture that emerges is fairly consistent · on the praise side: rooms that are clean and roomy in a condo style, a nice atmosphere, well equipped for long stays, a free pool and gym to use, free parking that's convenient and not a fight, a location near the Amata Nakorn estate within walking distance, attentive staff who respond quickly, a kitchenette to cook for yourself, and good value on monthly rates for long-stay guests · on the observation side: what comes up is a cigarette smell in certain rooms or areas marked as non-smoking, which you should ask to change rooms over if you encounter it, bathroom drains in some rooms that are slow enough you have to scoop the water out yourself, housekeeping knocking to clean in the morning around 8 without notice, and the fact that the location is on the industrial estate side, not by the beach and not a tourist district for anyone expecting a relaxed seaside vibe · on top of that, people without their own car may feel that getting around the estate area isn't as convenient as the city or Bangsaen Beach zone · these gripes are mostly about setting expectations correctly (a serviced apartment in an estate, not a seaside resort) and checking the room's condition and communicating clearly with staff before the stay, rather than big problems that keep people from coming back.

"Stayed three nights, the room was fine, good value, there's a pool you can use. My only gripe was the bathroom drain being a bit slow and a faint cigarette smell that lingered. I told the staff and they sorted it out. If you check the room well at check-in and report it right away, there's no real problem."

Comparing price and value — Patt sits in the accessible-price group for the Amata Nakorn–Chonburi area · daily rates for a Superior room start at about THB 720–850/night, from promo to regular pricing, while larger rooms like the Junior Suite and Family Suite step up to around THB 1,300–1,720/night depending on size and season · but what makes this place the best value is the monthly rate, which starts at about THB 9,000/month for long leases of 6 months or more, and sits around THB 15,000–18,000/month for a 1–2 month lease (with rates tiered by the number of months), which suits estate workers who need to live in Chonburi for several months very well, because the per-night cost drops far below booking by the day, and you get a pool, gym, parking and a room with a kitchenette ready to go · compared with serviced apartments and apartments of the same tier in the estate area, what gives Patt the edge is having a free pool and gym plus 34 sqm rooms that are spacious and well equipped at a price that isn't expensive · but you trade that against not being by the beach, having no sea view, and sitting in an industrial area · if the goal of your stay is "living long-term near work in the estate, with a clean, well-equipped room, a pool and gym, on a budget you can control", every baht you spend at Patt counts as money well returned · but if the goal is a beach trip or a relaxed seaside vibe, this location doesn't match that need, and you should choose accommodation on the Bangsaen or Pattaya side instead.

What to know before booking — a few things help the stay go more smoothly · one, if you plan to stay long-term for months, ask the property directly about the monthly rate (from about THB 9,000/month for a long lease) because it's far better value than booking continuous daily stays, and check what the price includes, such as water and electricity and weekly cleaning · two, at check-in you should check the room's condition thoroughly, especially the cigarette smell and the bathroom drain, and if you find a problem, tell staff right away to ask for a room change or a fix · three, if you work the night shift or want to sleep in, tell staff your preferred cleaning time or ask for a do-not-disturb sign right from check-in, because reviews mention housekeeping knocking in the morning around 8 · four, this is accommodation in the estate area, not by the beach, and suits people with a car; if you don't have a car, budget for transport and ride-hailing in the area · five, check whether the room you book has a kitchenette, fridge, microwave and bathtub as you want, because each room type (for example, the Junior Suite with/without a bathtub) is equipped differently · six, pick a free-cancellation option first if your plans aren't certain, and compare prices across several platforms (Agoda / Booking / Trip.com), as well as against booking directly with the property for the monthly rate, because prices can differ by channel.

Summary — from all the real reviews, Patt Serviced Apartments is the best fit for workers in the Amata Nakorn estate, company staff and engineers on multi-month projects, families relocating temporarily to Chonburi, and self-drivers who want a condo-style room with everything included at a manageable price · the strengths guests bring up consistently are clean, roomy rooms of around 34 sqm, a free pool and gym to use, convenient free parking, a kitchenette to cook for yourself in some rooms, and the value especially on the monthly rate, which makes it a good base for anyone who needs to be near work in the estate for many days or months · but you have to accept honestly that this place is on the industrial estate side, not by the beach, not a tourist district, and that some reviews mention a cigarette smell, bathroom drains and cleaning times you should communicate about clearly · if you're after a beachfront resort where you step out of your room onto the sand, or a relaxed seaside vibe, this may not be the answer, and you should consider accommodation on the Bangsaen or Pattaya side instead · but for a long stay near work in the Amata Nakorn estate, with a clean, well-equipped room, a pool and gym, and value on a budget you can control — Patt is a choice that meets that need well and on point.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Patt Serviced Apartments

faq.q: Where is Patt Serviced Apartments, and how close is it to the Amata Nakorn estate?
faq.a: Patt Serviced Apartments is at 471/249 Moo 5, Soi Thonglang, Khlong Tamru, Mueang Chon Buri, in the heart of Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate · from the property it's about a 15-minute walk to the Amata Nakorn estate, and Ninja Night Market is within walking distance · it's about a 15-minute drive to Central Chonburi, near the Bang Na–Trat (Burapha Withi) expressway connecting Bangkok–Pattaya–Rayong · it's about 40 km from Suvarnabhumi Airport (~50 min drive) and about 10 km from Chonburi train station.

faq.q: How much does Patt Serviced Apartments start at, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Daily rates start at about THB 720/night for a Superior Room of around 34 sqm · Junior Suite (with/without a bathtub) around THB 1,300 · Family Suite around THB 1,720 (prices move with the season) · the best value is the monthly rate from about THB 9,000/month for a long lease of 6 months or more, and around THB 15,000–18,000/month for 1–2 months · you should compare prices across several platforms (Agoda / Booking / Trip.com) and against booking directly with the property for the monthly rate.

faq.q: Who is Patt Serviced Apartments best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for workers in the Amata Nakorn estate, company staff and engineers on multi-month projects, families relocating temporarily to Chonburi, and self-drivers who want a condo-style room with everything included, a pool and gym, at a manageable price · it isn't a fit for people who want a beachfront resort, a relaxed seaside vibe, or those without a car who want to walk straight to the sights.

faq.q: Does Patt Serviced Apartments have a pool and parking?
faq.a: Yes — an outdoor pool (reviews say it's saltwater) and a gym open 6:00 AM–10:00 PM daily, free to use · there's free parking that many reviews say is convenient and not a fight · on top of that there's a clubhouse, a convenience store in the building, laundry service (paid), a 24-hour front desk, and free Wi-Fi in the rooms and common areas.

faq.q: Does Patt Serviced Apartments take daily or monthly stays, and is there a kitchen in the room?
faq.a: It takes both daily and monthly stays · daily from about THB 720/night and monthly from about THB 9,000/month and up depending on room type and lease length · many rooms have a fridge, microwave, satellite TV, safe, and some have a kitchenette with a sofa and dining nook, good for long stays and cooking for yourself · if you want a kitchenette or a bathtub, choose the right room type when booking, as each is equipped differently.

faq.q: Is there anything to watch out for before booking Patt Serviced Apartments?
faq.a: Some reviews note a cigarette smell in certain rooms, slow-draining bathrooms, and housekeeping knocking to clean in the morning around 8 without notice · we'd suggest checking the room's condition thoroughly at check-in, and if you find a smell or bathroom problem, tell staff right away to ask for a room change, and tell them your preferred cleaning time or ask for a do-not-disturb sign if you want to sleep in · on top of that, this place is on the industrial estate side, not by the beach, and suits people with a car more.
